description:
(Summary from jobright.ai; the original posting may say more.)

Northwood builds software for operating its global network of antenna ground stations and supporting cloud services. The role contributes to internal platform tools and systems for software delivery, testing, ground-station operations, observability, infrastructure, and security.
Full Stack Developer building CI/release and cloud-to-ground infrastructure, automating remote deployments, and developing fleet operations tools

Responsibilities:
• Build the CI and release pipelines that take code from commit to production, in the cloud and at ground stations around the world
• Make shipping safe and continuous, with staged rollouts and fast rollback, so no one has to test in production
• Build simulated ground stations and lab test benches running real hardware, so every release is tested against realistic conditions before it reaches a live site
• Build tools that replay real recorded data through the system to catch problems early
• Automate how new sites are brought online, configured, and updated, in remote locations with few or no people on site
• Write software that runs on the servers that sit next to the antennas, and keep a global fleet of them healthy
• Build the monitoring, logging, and alerting that show the health of every service and site
• Turn raw telemetry into signals engineers and operators can act on before a problem reaches a customer
• Build the backend services and web interfaces engineers and operators use every day to create, ship, and run software
• Talk directly with the people who use what you build, and turn their feedback into improvements
• Define the cloud and site infrastructure the platform runs on as code
• Build identity, secrets management, and least-privilege access into the platform, so every service gets them by default

Requirements:
• 0 to 2 years of professional software experience. It doesn't have to be a full-time role. Internships, research, open source, and projects outside the classroom all count, so tell us about them
• Bachelor's degree in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering, math, or a related field. This is a soft requirement: if you didn't pursue a degree, tell us what you did instead
• Has written real software in at least one general-purpose language (such as Python, Go, Rust, TypeScript, or C++) beyond required coursework
• Has built and shipped something other people used or relied on
• Has solved a hard technical problem largely on their own, such as debugging a non-obvious failure or designing a system from scratch
• you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State

Preferred:
• proficiency in one or more languages (such as Python, Go, Rust, or TypeScript), with opinions about which one fits which job
• has built a backend API and a frontend that uses it (such as a React app on a REST API)
• exposure to CI pipelines (such as GitHub Actions or GitLab CI), containers (such as Docker), a cloud platform (such as AWS), or infrastructure as code (such as Terraform or CloudFormation)
• day-to-day comfort with Linux and the command line, or coursework and projects in operating systems, networking, or distributed systems
• built a tool, script, or library other developers used
• projects involving hardware, embedded systems, RF, robotics, or space, such as a CubeSat, rocketry, or robotics team
• a track record of going past what was asked, such as side projects, competitions, research, or things built because you wanted to
• comfort with AI coding tools (such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor)
